# Sizing a power station for a fridge

You need to check three things: surge watts, continuous watts, and watt-hours (Wh).

**1. Surge watts (the one that most often causes problems).** The compressor briefly draws a large spike when it starts. Sources put this at roughly 1,000-2,400W depending on the fridge, and one sizing guide uses 1,300W as a safe allowance. Look for a station with a surge rating of at least 1,300W, and 2,000W+ for a large French-door or older fridge. The output should be pure sine wave. ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))

**2. Continuous watts.** A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250W, so almost any 1,000W-class station covers it. Add up anything else you'll run at the same time.

**3. Watt-hours (runtime).** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so the average draw is much lower than the label wattage.
- A typical ENERGY STAR full-size fridge averages about 41W, or roughly 1,000 Wh/day. With inverter losses and a 20% margin, plan on about **1,400 Wh per day**. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator))
- For your own fridge, take the kWh/year from its yellow EnergyGuide label, multiply by 1,000, and divide by 8,760. That gives average watts. Large side-by-sides with ice makers can use about double.
- Keep the door shut during the outage.

## Quick picks by outage length

| Outage | Capacity | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Up to about 12-17 hours | ~1,000 Wh | [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (1,152 Wh, 1,800W, 2,700W peak), $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF |
| About 24-33 hours | ~2,000 Wh | [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) (2,073 Wh), $899, or $854.05 with AFF5OFF; estimated 33.6 hours of fridge runtime |
| 2+ days | 3,000+ Wh | [BLUETTI Elite 300](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-300) (3,014 Wh), $1,099; estimated about 2 days |

The Anker SOLIX S2000 (2,010 Wh, 1,500W, 3,000W peak) is another 2 kWh-class option: [Anker's guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator).

The runtime estimates come from HomeGrid HQ's assumptions of a 150W fridge, 35% duty cycle, and 85% inverter efficiency. Your results will vary with room temperature and how often the door is opened.

## My suggestion
For most people, a **~2,000 Wh LiFePO4 unit** such as the Elite 200 V2 is the best balance: it covers about a day with margin and leaves room for a router and phone charging. If you only need to bridge a few hours, or can run the fridge intermittently, a ~1,000 Wh unit like the AC180 works.

A few caveats:
- The Dealectric links are affiliate links that open BLUETTI's official US store. Dealectric earns a commission, and the code is entered at checkout. Prices and codes come from that page and can change, so check them at checkout.
- Compact units under about 300-500 Wh, such as the Patriot Power Sidekick, typically fail the surge check.
- If you tell me your fridge's size or its EnergyGuide kWh/year figure and how long your outages usually last, I can narrow this down.
